questions.question: Which of the following organisations launched the 'Digital Taxpayer Interface System' (DTIS) in 2025 to ease income tax filing?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Central Board of Direct Taxes (CBDT)**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Central Board of Direct Taxes (CBDT)** officially launched the **Digital Taxpayer Interface System (DTIS)** in **2025** as a major step toward digitizing tax administration.
 
• The primary objective of **DTIS** is to simplify the **Income Tax filing** process for both individual and corporate taxpayers by providing a more intuitive and user-friendly interface.
 
• The system integrates **Artificial Intelligence (AI)** and **Data Analytics** to provide **pre-filled tax forms**, which significantly reduces errors and the time required for **Income Tax Return (ITR)** submission.
 
• Through **DTIS**, the **CBDT** aims to enhance **transparency** and **accountability** in the tax ecosystem, ensuring that taxpayers can track their refunds and notice statuses in real-time.
 
• This initiative is part of the broader **Digital India** vision, focusing on "Minimum Government, Maximum Governance" by reducing the need for physical interaction between taxpayers and **tax authorities**. ***Hence, the correct answer is Central Board of Direct Taxes (CBDT).***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Central Board of Direct Taxes (CBDT):**

 
 
• The **CBDT** is a **statutory authority** functioning under the **Central Board of Revenue Act, 1963**.
 
• It is a part of the **Department of Revenue** under the **Ministry of Finance**, Government of India.
 
• It provides essential inputs for policy and planning of **direct taxes** in India and is responsible for the administration of direct tax laws through the **Income Tax Department**.
 
• The board is headed by a **Chairman** and comprises **six members**, each responsible for different domains such as **Income Tax & Revenue**, **Legislation & Computerization**, and **Investigation**.
 
 
 
• **Direct vs. Indirect Taxes:**
 
 
• **Direct Taxes** are levied directly on the income or wealth of individuals and organizations. Examples include **Income Tax** and **Corporate Tax**. These are managed by the **CBDT**.
 
• **Indirect Taxes** are levied on goods and services rather than income. The **GST Council** and the **Central Board of Indirect Taxes and Customs (CBIC)** oversee these taxes, including **GST**, **Customs Duty**, and **Excise Duty**.
 
 
 
• **NITI Aayog:**
 
 
• Established on **January 1, 2015**, replacing the Planning Commission, it serves as the premier **policy think tank** of the Government of India.
 
• It provides **directional and policy inputs** but does not handle the collection or administration of taxes.
 
 
 
• **Reserve Bank of India (RBI):**
 
 
• The **RBI** is India's **central bank**, established on **April 1, 1935**, under the **RBI Act, 1934**.
 
• Its primary functions include **monetary policy**, regulation of the **banking sector**, and managing **foreign exchange**, rather than direct tax administration.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Income Tax Act, 1961:** This is the fundamental statute that governs the levy, administration, collection, and recovery of **Income Tax** in India.
 
• **Taxpayers' Charter:** Introduced by the **CBDT** in **2020**, it defines the commitment of the **Income Tax Department** towards taxpayers, emphasizing **courtesy**, **fairness**, and **reasonableness**.
 
• **E-filing 2.0:** Before the launch of **DTIS**, the **Income Tax Department** utilized the **E-filing 2.0 portal** to facilitate electronic filing, which laid the technological groundwork for more advanced systems.
 
• **Permanent Account Number (PAN):** A **ten-digit alphanumeric identifier** issued by the **Income Tax Department**, which is mandatory for filing tax returns and tracking financial transactions under the **DTIS**.

questions.question: In 2025, which nation announced its withdrawal from the Economic Community of Central African States (ECCAS)?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Rwanda**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In **January 2025**, the government of **Rwanda** officially announced its decision to withdraw from the **Economic Community of Central African States (ECCAS)**, also known by its French acronym **CEEAC**.
 
• This decision marks the second time **Rwanda** has exited the bloc; the nation originally left in **2008** to focus on its integration within the **East African Community (EAC)** and **COMESA**, only to rejoin **ECCAS** in **2016**.
 
• The withdrawal is part of a broader strategic shift by **Kigali** to rationalize its memberships in **Regional Economic Communities (RECs)**, citing the need to avoid overlapping mandates and the financial burden of multiple membership dues.
 
• The move comes at a time of heightened regional tensions in the **Great Lakes region**, particularly involving **Rwanda**, the **Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC)**, and **Burundi**, which are all prominent members of the organization. ***Hence, the correct answer is Rwanda.***
 
• The **ECCAS** Secretariat was formally notified of the decision, which triggers a transition period as per the organization's revised treaty guidelines.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **About ECCAS:**
 
 
• The **Economic Community of Central African States (ECCAS)** was established in **October 1983** and began functioning in **1985**.
 
• The headquarters of the organization is located in **Libreville, Gabon**.
 
• Prior to **Rwanda's** 2025 withdrawal, the bloc comprised **11 member states**: **Angola, Burundi, Cameroon, Central African Republic, Chad, Congo, DR Congo, Equatorial Guinea, Gabon, Rwanda, and Sao Tome and Principe**.
 
• The primary objective of **ECCAS** is to promote regional economic cooperation and establish a **Central African Common Market**.
 
 
 
• **Rwanda's Regional Affiliations:**
 
 
• **Rwanda** remains a highly active member of the **East African Community (EAC)**, which it joined in **2007**. The **EAC** is considered one of the most integrated regional blocs in **Africa**.
 
• The nation is also a member of the **Common Market for Eastern and Southern Africa (COMESA)**, which facilitates trade across a vast portion of the continent.
 
• **Rwanda** joined the **Commonwealth of Nations** in **2009**, despite having no historical colonial ties to the **United Kingdom**, reflecting its diverse diplomatic outreach.
 
 
 
• **Economic Integration Challenges:**
 
 
• The **African Union (AU)** has often encouraged member states to limit "multiple memberships" in various **RECs** to streamline the implementation of the **African Continental Free Trade Area (AfCFTA)**.
 
• **ECCAS** has faced significant hurdles in integration due to persistent conflicts in the **Congo Basin** and varying levels of economic development among its **Central African** members.
 
• The **2019 institutional reform** of **ECCAS** aimed to transform the General Secretariat into a **Commission** to enhance its executive powers and efficiency in conflict resolution.
 
 
</ul

questions.question: Which of the following portals integrated multiple agriculture schemes across ministries in June 2025?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Krishi Nivesh**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Krishi Nivesh** portal was integrated in **June 2025** to serve as a comprehensive, one-stop platform for multiple agriculture-related schemes across various ministries of the **Government of India**.
 
• It was designed to facilitate **Ease of Doing Business** in the agricultural sector by streamlining the application process for various government incentives and subsidies.
 
• The portal brings together schemes from the **Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare**, the **Ministry of Food Processing Industries**, and other allied departments to promote **Agri-infrastructure** and **investment**.
 
• It aims to provide a seamless interface for **Agri-entrepreneurs**, **Farmer Producer Organizations (FPOs)**, and **cooperatives** to access central and state government benefits through a single window.
 
• By integrating multiple digital platforms, **Krishi Nivesh** reduces the **turnaround time** for project approvals and enhances the **transparency** of the fund disbursement process.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Scope of Integration:** The portal covers a wide range of programs, including the **Agriculture Infrastructure Fund (AIF)**, the **National Livestock Mission**, and the **Mission for Integrated Development of Horticulture (MIDH)**.
 
• **Target Beneficiaries:** It primarily targets **Individual Farmers**, **Startups**, **Micro, Small, and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs)**, and large-scale **Agri-businesses** looking to invest in the rural economy.
 
• **Digital Infrastructure:** The **Krishi Nivesh** portal utilizes **Real-time Analytics** and **Project Tracking** features to help the government monitor the implementation of schemes at the **District** and **State** levels.
 
• **Economic Impact:** The integration is expected to boost **domestic investment** and **Foreign Direct Investment (FDI)** in the post-harvest management and processing sectors, leading to better **value addition** for farmers' produce.
 
• **User Accessibility:** The platform provides detailed information on eligibility criteria, necessary documentation, and **financial assistance** limits for each integrated scheme in multiple regional languages.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Convergence of Schemes:** One of the primary objectives of the portal in **2025** is to ensure **Convergence**, preventing the duplication of efforts across different government departments.
 
• **Application Lifecycle:** Once a user registers on **Krishi Nivesh**, they are provided with a **Unique Tracking ID**, which allows them to monitor their application status from submission to the **Sanction of Funds**.
 
• **Nodal Agency:** The **Ministry of Agriculture** acts as the primary oversight body, ensuring that the portal remains updated with the latest **Policy Guidelines** and interest subvention rates.
 
• **Agri-Sops:** The portal also highlights specific **Sops** (incentives) provided for **Organic Farming**, **Precision Agriculture**, and the **Digital Agriculture Mission**.
</ul

questions.question: What is the name of the scheme announced in Union Budget 2025–26 for promoting Indian language books in digital form?

questions.question: The World Social Summit (Second Summit for Social Development) was scheduled for 4–6 November 2025 in:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Doha, Qatar**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **United Nations General Assembly** has decided to convene the **Second World Summit for Social Development**, which is scheduled to be held in **Doha, Qatar**.
 
• The summit is slated to take place from **4 to 6 November 2025**, marking a significant milestone in global social policy.
 
• The decision to hold this summit was formalized through **UN General Assembly resolution 78/173**, which emphasizes the need to address emerging challenges in social development.
 
• The primary objective of the **2025 Summit** is to evaluate progress made since the inaugural summit and to recommit to the principles of social justice and equity.
 
• It aims to provide a renewed momentum for the implementation of the **Copenhagen Declaration on Social Development** and the **Programme of Action**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **The First World Summit for Social Development:**
 
 
• The **First World Summit** was held in **Copenhagen, Denmark**, in **March 1995**.
 
• It was the largest gathering of world leaders at that time specifically focused on social development issues.
 
• The summit resulted in the **Copenhagen Declaration**, where **117 heads of state** pledged to make **poverty eradication**, **full employment**, and **social integration** the overriding objectives of development.
 
 
 
• **Alignment with the 2030 Agenda:**
 
 
• The **Second World Summit** in **Doha** is strategically aligned with the **Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs)** of the **2030 Agenda**.
 
• It seeks to address the "missing link" in global development by focusing on human-centric policies that ensure no one is left behind.
 
• Current global crises, including the aftermath of the **COVID-19 pandemic**, economic instability, and climate change, have necessitated this high-level meeting.
 
 
 
• **The Role of Qatar:**
 
 
• **Qatar** has increasingly become a hub for international diplomacy and high-level **United Nations** conferences.
 
• Hosting the summit in **Doha** highlights the **Middle East's** growing influence in shaping global social and economic discourse.
 
• The summit is expected to produce a **political declaration** that will guide international efforts for the next decade.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Key Themes:** The summit will focus on **social protection systems**, **decent work**, and **reducing inequalities** within and among countries.
 
• **Poverty Eradication:** A central pillar remains the **eradication of poverty** in all its forms and dimensions, which is **SDG 1**.
 
• **Global Social Contract:** Discussions are expected to revolve around the concept of a **"New Global Social Contract"** proposed by the **UN Secretary-General** in the **"Our Common Agenda"** report.
 
• **Preparatory Process:** The **United Nations Department of Economic and Social Affairs (UN DESA)** is playing a lead role in the preparatory stages, ensuring inclusive participation from **civil society** and **non-governmental organizations**.
</ul

questions.question: Which of the following reports, released in October 2025, stated that human‑caused PM2.5 pollution was responsible for more than 1.7 million deaths in India in 2022?

options.text: The UNEP Global Assessment Report on Air Pollution and Health
The Lancet Countdown on Health and Climate Change
The World Health Organization Air Quality Assessment Report, 2025
India State of Environment and Health Overview Report, 2025

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**The Lancet Countdown on Health and Climate Change**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The Lancet Countdown on Health and Climate Change** released its global report in **October 2024/2025**, highlighting the severe impacts of **air pollution** and **climate change** on human mortality.
 
• According to the report, **human-caused PM2.5 pollution** was responsible for more than **1.7 million deaths** in **India** during the year **2022**.
 
• The assessment indicates that the burning of **fossil fuels** (like **coal** and **oil**) is the primary driver of this toxic **particulate matter**, which penetrates deep into the **respiratory system**.
 
• The report emphasizes that **global health** is being threatened by the continued use of **dirty energy**, leading to a rise in **respiratory diseases**, **strokes**, and **heart attacks**.
 
• In the context of **India**, the report notes that air pollution levels consistently exceed **World Health Organization (WHO)** guidelines, making it one of the most affected countries **globally**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Understanding PM2.5:**
 
 
• **PM2.5** refers to **particulate matter** with a diameter of less than **2.5 micrometers**, which is about **3%** of the diameter of a human hair.
 
• Due to its small **size**, it can travel deep into the **lungs** and enter the **bloodstream**, causing systemic health issues.
 
• Major **sources** in **India** include **vehicle emissions**, **industrial combustion**, **crop burning**, and **construction dust**.
 
 
 
• **The Lancet Countdown:**
 
 
• It is an **international**, multidisciplinary collaboration that monitors the emerging health profiles of **climate change**.
 
• It tracks over **50 indicators** across **five key domains**, including health impacts, adaptation, and **mitigation actions**.
 
• The collaboration includes experts from **University College London (UCL)** and over **50 other academic institutions** and **UN agencies**.
 
 
 
• **Health Impacts in India:**
 
 
• Aside from **PM2.5**, **India** is witnessing a surge in **heat-related mortality**, with deaths among people over **age 65** increasing significantly over the last **decade**.
 
• The report also warns about the increasing suitability for the transmission of infectious **diseases** like **Dengue** and **Malaria** due to changing **climatic conditions**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Economic Burden:** The **1.7 million deaths** in **2022** also translated into massive **economic losses** for **India**, equivalent to a significant percentage of its **GDP** due to lost productivity and **healthcare costs**.
 
• **Global Context:** Globally, the report highlighted that **deaths** attributed to **fossil fuel-derived PM2.5** have seen varying trends, but **India** remains a **hotspot** for **pollution-related mortality**.
 
• **Policy Recommendations:** The **Lancet Countdown** advocates for a rapid transition to **renewable energy** (like **solar** and **wind**) to achieve **net-zero emissions** and save millions of lives.
 
• **Data Fact:** In **India**, the **National Clean Air Programme (NCAP)** was launched in **2019** to reduce **particulate matter** concentration by **20-30%** by **2024** (later revised to **40%** by **2026**), yet challenges remain in meeting these **targets**.
</ul

questions.question: As reported in February 2025, the Union Environment Ministry of Government of India developed new features on which platform for quicker processing of forest clearances?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**PARIVESH 2.0**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In **February 2025**, the **Union Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change (MoEFCC)** introduced enhanced features on the **PARIVESH 2.0** platform to streamline and accelerate the processing of **forest clearances**.
 
• The **PARIVESH 2.0** portal functions as a **Single-Window Integrated Environmental Management System**, providing a unified interface for project proponents to apply for **Environment, Forest, Wildlife, and CRZ** clearances.
 
• The new updates focus on the **digital transformation** of the appraisal process, minimizing physical touchpoints and reducing the **turnaround time** for approvals related to **infrastructure and industrial projects**.
 
• The platform integrates a **Geographic Information System (GIS)** based decision support tool, which allows authorities to analyze **geospatial data**, forest density, and proximity to protected areas with higher precision.
 
• By automating **stage-wise monitoring**, the system ensures **accountability** and **transparency** in the decision-making process between the **State Forest Departments** and the **Central Government**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Understanding PARIVESH:** 
 
 
• The acronym stands for **Pro-Active and Responsive facilitation by Interactive, Virtuous and Environmental Single-window Hub**.
 
• It was initially launched in **August 2018** by the **Government of India** to simplify the regulatory landscape for environmental approvals.
 
• The transition to **PARIVESH 2.0** represents a shift toward **Next-Generation technology**, incorporating **Data Analytics** and **Cloud-based infrastructure** for better data management.
 
 
 
• **Regulatory Framework:** 
 
 
• Forest clearances are primarily governed by the **Forest (Conservation) Act, 1980**, which mandates prior central approval for the diversion of forest land for non-forestry purposes.
 
• The portal helps in the enforcement of the **Environment (Protection) Act, 1986** and the **Wildlife (Protection) Act, 1972** by ensuring all projects meet statutory environmental norms.
 
 
 
• **Integration with National Initiatives:** 
 
 
• The platform is closely linked with the **PM Gati Shakti National Master Plan**, aimed at integrated planning and coordinated implementation of **infrastructure connectivity projects** across **India**.
 
• It supports the **Ease of Doing Business** index by providing **real-time tracking** of applications and **automatic alerts** via SMS and email to stakeholders.
 
 
 
• **Technical Development:** 
 
 
• The portal is designed and developed by the **National Informatics Centre (NIC)** in collaboration with the **MoEFCC**.
 
• It utilizes **Remote Sensing** data to verify the status of compensatory afforestation land and existing green cover.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Impact on Timelines:** Before the implementation of such digital hubs, environmental and forest clearances often took over **600 days**; however, the **PARIVESH** workflow has significantly reduced this to less than **180 days** for many categories.
 
• **Scope of Clearances:** 
 
 
• **Environment Clearance (EC):** Required for projects listed in the **EIA Notification, 2006**.
 
• **Forest Clearance (FC):** Required for projects involving any **forest land**.
 
• **Wildlife Clearance (WC):** Mandatory if a project is located within or near a **National Park** or **Wildlife Sanctuary**.
 
• **CRZ Clearance:** Necessary for projects in **Coastal Regulation Zones**.
 
 
 
• **User Accessibility:** The system provides a **Common Application Form (CAF)**, ensuring that users do not have to enter the same project details multiple times for different types of clearances.
</ul

questions.question: What is the full form of ICC in the context of cricket?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**International Cricket Council**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **International Cricket Council (ICC)** is the global governing body for the sport of **cricket**, overseeing international competitions and ranking systems.
 
• It was originally founded as the **Imperial Cricket Conference** on **15 June 1909** by representatives from **England, Australia,** and **South Africa**.
 
• The organization underwent a name change in **1965** to become the **International Cricket Conference**, before finally adopting its current name, the **International Cricket Council**, in **1987**.
 
• The primary role of the **ICC** is to organize major world championship events, most notably the **ICC Men's Cricket World Cup**, the **ICC T20 World Cup**, and the **ICC World Test Championship**.
 
• The **ICC** is also responsible for the appointment of **Umpires** and **Match Referees** who officiate at all sanctioned **Test matches**, **One Day Internationals (ODIs)**, and **Twenty20 Internationals**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Headquarters**: For nearly a century, the **ICC** was headquartered at **Lord's Cricket Ground** in **London**. However, in **August 2005**, it moved its **headquarters** to **Dubai, United Arab Emirates**, primarily for tax reasons and to be more centrally located among its global members.
 
• **Membership**: The **ICC** currently has **108 member nations**. This includes **12 Full Members** who play **Test matches** and **96 Associate Members** who participate in various qualifying structures.
 
• **Full Members**: These include nations like **India, Australia, England, Pakistan, South Africa, New Zealand, West Indies, Sri Lanka, Bangladesh, Zimbabwe, Ireland,** and **Afghanistan**.
 
• **BCCI Relation**: In the context of India, the **Board of Control for Cricket in India (BCCI)** is the national governing body that represents India at the **ICC**. Option 4, **Indian Cricket Council**, is often confused with the **BCCI**.
 
• **Leadership**: The **ICC** is led by a **Chairman** and a **Chief Executive Officer (CEO)**. For example, **Greg Barclay** took office as the **Chairman** in **2020**, and **Geoff Allardice** serves as the **CEO**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Laws of Cricket**: While the **ICC** administers the game, it does not actually own the **copyright** to the **Laws of Cricket**. The **Marylebone Cricket Club (MCC)** in **London** remains the custodian and author of the laws, though the **ICC** develops the **Standard Playing Conditions** for international matches.
 
• **Integrity and Ethics**: The **ICC** operates an **Anti-Corruption Unit (ACU)** to combat match-fixing and spot-fixing, ensuring the **integrity** of the sport remains intact globally.
 
• **Development**: The **ICC Development Program** aims to grow the game in non-traditional cricket-playing regions, providing funding and infrastructure support to **Associate Members**.
 
• **Revenue Model**: The **ICC** generates significant **revenue** through the sale of broadcasting rights for its major events, which is then distributed among its member nations to support the growth of the game at the grassroots level.
</ul

questions.question: Which of the following cities of India established a Public-Private Partnership (PPP) model-based green waste processing plant under the Swachh Bharat Mission-Urban that started the first batch of trial production in March 2025?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Indore**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The city of **Indore**, located in **Madhya Pradesh**, has established a state-of-the-art **green waste processing plant** based on the **Public-Private Partnership (PPP)** model under the **Swachh Bharat Mission-Urban (SBM-U)**.
 
• This facility commenced its **first batch of trial production** in **March 2025**, marking a significant milestone in urban waste management and circular economy initiatives.
 
• The plant is designed to process **horticultural waste**, such as tree prunings, leaves, and garden trimmings, which were previously a challenge to manage in traditional composting units.
 
• Under the **PPP model**, the **Indore Municipal Corporation (IMC)** provided the land at the **Devguradia** waste disposal site, while the private partner invested in the machinery and technology for processing.
 
• The output of this green waste plant includes **bio-coal** or **high-quality briquettes**, which serve as a sustainable alternative to fossil fuels in industrial boilers and furnaces.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• It focuses on **source segregation** of solid waste, utilizing the **3Rs (Reduce, Reuse, Recycle)** principle, and scientific processing of all types of municipal solid waste.
 
 
 
• **Indore's Waste Management Success**:
 
 
• **Indore** has been recognized as **India's Cleanest City** for **seven consecutive years** (as of 2023-24) in the **Swachh Survekshan** rankings conducted by the **Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs**.
 
• The city is famous for its **100% waste segregation** at source into six categories: dry, wet, plastic, e-waste, domestic hazardous, and sanitary waste.
 
• It also hosts the **Gobar-Dhan Bio-CNG plant**, which is **Asia's largest** municipal solid waste-based Bio-CNG facility, inaugurated in **February 2022**.
 
 
 
• **Green Waste and Circular Economy**:
 
 
• Green waste processing helps in reducing the burden on **landfills** and prevents the open burning of garden waste, which is a major cause of **air pollution**.
 
• By converting organic waste into **bio-energy** or **compost**, cities contribute to the **Net Zero** targets and promote the **Circular Economy** framework.
 
• The **PPP model** in waste management ensures **operational efficiency**, **technological innovation**, and **financial sustainability** for urban local bodies.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

• **Capacity**: The **Indore green waste plant** is expected to handle approximately **50 to 100 tonnes** of horticultural waste daily, significantly enhancing the city's overall waste processing capacity.

questions.question: Under the scheme ADITI (Acing Development of Innovative Technologies), announced at DefConnect 2024, which of the following is the size of the corpus to promote innovation in defence technologies?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**₹750 crore**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The Union Minister of Defence, **Shri Rajnath Singh**, launched the **ADITI** (Acing Development of Innovative Technologies) scheme during the **DefConnect 2024** event held in **New Delhi** on **March 4, 2024**.
 
• The scheme has been allocated a significant corpus of **₹750 crore** for the period **2023-24 to 2025-26** to foster innovation in **critical and strategic defence technologies**.
 
• **ADITI** falls under the **iDEX** (Innovations for Defence Excellence) framework, which is managed by the **Department of Defence Production** within the **Ministry of Defence**.
 
• The primary objective of the scheme is to develop approximately **30 deep-tech critical technologies** that are essential for the **Indian Armed Forces**, thereby reducing reliance on imports.
 
• Under this scheme, eligible **start-ups** can receive a grant-in-aid of up to **₹25 crore** for their research and development efforts in the field of defence technology.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **iDEX (Innovations for Defence Excellence):** Launched in **April 2018**, iDEX aims to create an ecosystem to foster innovation and technology development in **Defence and Aerospace** by engaging industries, including **MSMEs**, **start-ups**, and individual innovators.
 
• **Defence Innovation Organisation (DIO):** The iDEX scheme is funded and managed by the **DIO**, which is a **Section 8** company formed by two major Defence Public Sector Undertakings (DPSUs): **Hindustan Aeronautics Limited (HAL)** and **Bharat Electronics Limited (BEL)**.
 
• **Aatmanirbharta in Defence:** The ADITI scheme is a pivotal step toward achieving **Aatmanirbhar Bharat** (self-reliant India) in the defence sector, ensuring that the country's security requirements are met through **indigenous technology**.
 
• **DefConnect 2024:** This event served as a platform for **start-ups**, **investors**, and **policymakers** to collaborate; it also saw the launch of the **11th edition** of the **Defence India Start-up Challenge (DISC)**.
 
• **Technology Domains:** The scheme focuses on high-end technologies such as **Artificial Intelligence (AI)**, **Quantum Technology**, **Robotics**, **Space-based systems**, and **Cybersecurity** for the military.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **ADITI Challenges:** In its first edition, the scheme launched **17 challenges** covering various requirements of the **Indian Army**, **Indian Navy**, **Indian Air Force**, and the **Defence Space Agency**.
 
• **Grant Structure:** The grant of **₹25 crore** is designed to support **deep-tech** projects that require substantial capital investment and long-term research cycles, which are often difficult for small start-ups to fund independently.
 
• **Monitoring and Support:** The **Ministry of Defence** provides not just financial assistance but also **mentorship** and **trial/testing facilities** to ensure the developed technologies meet the rigorous standards of the **Armed Forces**.
 
• **Impact on Economy:** By promoting a robust **defence industrial base**, the scheme aims to transform India from a **major importer** of defence equipment to a **global exporter** of advanced military hardware.

questions.question: Who won the Men’s Singles title at the Australian Open 2025?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Jannik Sinner**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Jannik Sinner** emerged as the champion of the **Men’s Singles** category at the **Australian Open 2025**. This victory marked his **second consecutive** title at the Melbourne-based Grand Slam, following his maiden win in **2024**.
 
• In the final match held on **January 26, 2025**, at the **Rod Laver Arena**, Sinner defeated **Alexander Zverev** in straight sets (6–4, 6–4, 6–2). This triumph solidified his status as the **World No. 1** in the **ATP Rankings**.
 
• The **Italian** tennis star demonstrated exceptional form throughout the tournament, reaching the final by defeating **Carlos Alcaraz** in a high-stakes semi-final encounter. ***Hence, the mention of Jannik Sinner as the winner is correct.***
 
• By winning this title, Sinner became one of the few players in the **Open Era** to successfully defend his first Grand Slam title at the very next edition of the same tournament.
 
• The **Australian Open 2025** was the **113th edition** of the tournament and the first **Grand Slam** event of the calendar year.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Jannik Sinner:**
 
 
• Born in **San Candido, Italy**, in **2001**, Sinner is known for his powerful baseline play and mental composure.
 
• He is the first **Italian player** to reach the top of the **ATP Rankings** and has now secured **three Grand Slam** titles (Australian Open 2024, US Open 2024, and Australian Open 2025).
 
• He is coached by the renowned **Darren Cahill** and **Simone Vagnozzi**, who have been instrumental in his rapid ascent in professional tennis.
 
 
 
• **Alexander Zverev:**
 
 
• The **German** professional, **Alexander Zverev**, was the runner-up in the **2025** edition. This was his second major Grand Slam final appearance in two years, having previously reached the final of **Roland Garros in 2024**.
 
• Zverev is an **Olympic Gold Medalist** (Tokyo 2020) and has won multiple **ATP Masters 1000** titles.
 
 
 
• **Australian Open Tournament:**
 
 
• Established in **1905**, it is the first of the four annual **Grand Slam** tennis tournaments, followed by the French Open, Wimbledon, and the US Open.
 
• The tournament moved from **Kooyong** to its current home at **Melbourne Park** in **1988**, coinciding with the switch from grass courts to **Hard Courts**.
 
• The **Men’s Singles** winner is awarded the **Norman Brookes Challenge Cup**, named after the former Australian tennis champion.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Prize Money:** The total prize pool for the **2025 Australian Open** saw a significant increase, with the singles winners receiving approximately **AUD 3.15 million**.
 
• **Surface Technology:** The matches are played on **GreenSet**, a brand of acrylic hard-court surface known for its medium-fast pace and consistent bounce.
 
• **Novak Djokovic's Record:** While Sinner is the current champion, **Novak Djokovic** holds the all-time record for the most Australian Open Men’s Singles titles, with **10 trophies**.
 
• **Historical Context:** Before the **Open Era** began in **1968**, the tournament was known as the **Australasian Championships** and later the Australian Championships.
